MTV Generation
EM-tee-vee jen-uh-RAY-shun
noun (Gen X slang)
From MTV (Music Television), the American cable channel that went on the air at 12:01 a.m. on August 1, 1981, with the words "Ladies and gentlemen, rock and roll" and, as its first video, the Buggles’ "Video Killed the Radio Star." By the late 1980s and early 1990s journalists and marketers were using MTV generation for the young Americans raised on the channel — roughly Generation X — and for the quick-cut editing, short attention spans, and image-driven culture it was blamed for. The label and Generation X (Douglas Coupland’s novel, 1991) became near-synonyms.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The MTV generation was the first to grow up with music you watched: three-minute videos, quick cuts, fashion and fantasy laid over every song, and a channel that never stopped. Critics said it shortened attention spans and turned pop stars into images; fans said it was the most exciting thing on television. Both were partly right. The Christian observation begins with the word generation, which in Scripture is always a question of what one generation hands to the next. The saddest verse in Judges is about a generation raised on something other than the knowledge of God: "there arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel" (Jdg 2:10). The faithful pattern is the reverse: "We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD" (Psa 78:4); "One generation shall praise thy works to another" (Psa 145:4). A generation is named for what discipled it. If MTV discipled Gen X more than the church or the home did, the name is an indictment, not a joke. The channel also trained the eye, and the Lord taught that "The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light" (Mat 6:22). Proverbs warns that "the eyes of man are never satisfied" (Pro 27:20), and an image a second can never satisfy them. A Gen X father can laugh at the old videos with his children and then do what his own culture often did not: show the generation to come the praises of the LORD.

Webster 1828 Definition

Label (late 1980s–90s) for the young Americans raised on MTV (launched August 1, 1981) and its quick-cut image culture; Scripture names a generation by what discipled it (Jdg 2:10) and charges each to show the next the praises of the LORD (Psa 78:4).

MTV GENERATION, n. (Gen X slang, late 1980s–1990s, US) The generation that came of age with MTV, roughly Generation X; also the fast-cut, image-driven, short-attention culture associated with it. "The MTV generation can’t sit through a three-hour movie."

MTV launched August 1, 1981; first video: the Buggles, "Video Killed the Radio Star"; VJs, video premieres, Headbangers Ball, Yo! MTV Raps.

Near-synonyms: Generation X (Coupland, 1991), slackers, latchkey kids.

Webster 1828: GENERATION, n. The act of begetting; procreation, as of animals. 1. Production; formation; as the generation of sounds or of curves or equations. 2. A single succession in natural descent, as the children of the same parents; hence, an age. Thus we say, the third, the fourth, or the tenth generation Genesis 15:16. …

Decode for parents: a generation is named for what discipled it; make sure yours is named for something better than a channel.

Key Scripture

Jdg 2:10 — "And also all that generation were gathered unto their fathers: and there arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel."

Psa 78:4 — "We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done."

Psa 145:4 — "One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts."

Mat 6:22 — "The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light."

Pro 27:20 — "Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied."

Modern Corruption

MTV generation names a people discipled by a channel; Scripture names generations by whether they knew the LORD and charges each to hand His praises to the next.

expand to see more

Discipled by a screen. Every generation is taught by something. For many children of the 1980s, the most consistent teacher in the house was the television, and MTV was its most persuasive voice: what to wear, what to want, what to think was cool. That is how Judges 2:10 happens — not by persecution, but by parents who assume the faith will be absorbed and a culture that teaches something else every afternoon. A generation that knew not the LORD is usually a generation nobody told.

One generation to another. The remedy is old and simple. Fathers and mothers declare God’s works to their children (Psa 78:4; Psa 145:4), on purpose, at the table and on the road. The eye must be made single (Mat 6:22), fixed on one Light rather than flickering after every image; the eyes of man are never satisfied otherwise (Pro 27:20). The MTV generation can still become the generation that broke the pattern. Gen X parents know the cost of the old pattern better than anyone, and that knowledge can become their gift to their children.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin generatio (a begetting) → generation → MTV (August 1, 1981) → MTV generation (late 1980s–90s) → synonym of Gen X; Scripture: shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD (Psa 78:4).

Latin generatio — a begetting; English generation — those born in one period

August 1, 1981: MTV launches with "Video Killed the Radio Star"

1980s: VJs, video premieres, the quick-cut style spreads to ads and films

Late 1980s–early 1990s: MTV generation as a label for Gen X

Biblical generations: one that knew not the LORD (Jdg 2:10); one that declares His works (Psa 145:4)
